utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you, Mr. Kereakes, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. First, before I ask the witness any questions, looking at the transcript yesterday, when the witness reviewed a witness statement he had taken, which was behind tab A of the package, I did not put the ERN numbers on the record of the pages he looked at, which I should have done. That witness statement is numbered 03230793 through 0803.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think if we can we should go into private session now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you could remember now, please, Mr. Kereakes, just to use the name "witness" for the person that we are talking about. Did you show this witness any photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which ones did you show him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: U-1 and U-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you tell us briefly - I know you have done it before - the procedures you followed when you showed the witness the line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At this time I would place the photo line-up on a table, escort the witness in a room. At which time I would instruct him to look at each picture, take his time. And to circle the number of the suspect that either caused him harm or detained him in the detention centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did the witness recognise or pick out anybody from the photographs in U-1 or U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell me about U-1, what did the witness do.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Positively identified Isak Musliu as the suspect that he had named.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness positively identified Fatmir Limaj as the suspect in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you include that in the witness statement that you took?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you have the witness sign U-1 and U-2 in this case?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you do with the photo line-up sheets U-1 and U-2 after the interview was over?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I then attached them to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Initially was the statement you took handwritten or typed?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when was the typed statement -- excuse me, created from the handwritten statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I had returned back to the CCIU office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the typewritten statement is verbatim word for word what was in your handwritten statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be small adjustments maybe that I would have made in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because sometimes I take the notes shorthand. Like instead of putting suspect photo line-up, maybe I would put photo line-up, U-1. Instead of putting suspect number 1, maybe I would just put the number symbol and 1. Maybe with a S next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when you took that handwritten statement and typed it up, did you have the witness sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my notes were in English, so I wouldn't have a witness sign a statement in English in a language that he didn't understand. So the procedure was, I would take the -- take the statement in my handwritten notes, type it up and then I would ask him to come in -- or once I had it translated, then I would have him sign it in his native language.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I would like you to look at the statement, again not saying the name, which is at tab 6, of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For the record, this is 03231247 through 1261. And I should say the previous statement we referred to, I again forgot to put the numbers in, 03231050 to 1054.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at -- have you found that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you please look at handwritten page 10, the last page of your notes. If I direct your attention to the bottom right-hand corner, do you see where it is written: "U-1, number 4 looks familiar. Not sure."

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember writing that in the notes during the interview?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you now go to page 4 of the typewritten statement. It has a number at the top 03231251, if that helps you find it.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: See towards the bottom of the page there, it states: I viewed line-up number 1, and number 4 looks familiar as being -- it should be Lapusnik, but I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you explain the difference between the typewritten sentence we've just looked at which has the additional words "as being at Lapusnik." That's not in your handwritten sentence.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a question I had asked him though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you explain that a little bit more. You asked him what question?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I asked these photo line-ups if it had nothing to do with the detention centre at Lapusnik, so that would be very -- that would be in response to the initial question of asking him to view the line-up and tell me if he had seen the suspects at Lapusnik, were these the suspects that beat him, depending on what the witness had told me, so that that makes a lot of sense, that I would have that in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again, if you look at the typewritten statement, he specifically on pages 2 and 3, there appear to be numerous handwritten corrections. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you make those corrections? Do you know what these are?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. What happened in this, the witness -- I hadn't made the appointment yet, but I had soon -- if you look at the date, I had soon left CCIU soon after that, and the witness wasn't available to come in and sign the statement, so the colleagues of mine who took over the case brought him in, had him review it, you know, and he made the changes on the Albanian statement which were then also made on the -- changes on the English statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to object. Lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't catch the basis of the objection, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Lack of foundation, lack of knowledge with regards to the testimony of this witness with regard to what other people did when apparently he was gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I will ask a few further question, Your Honour, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you present when these corrections were made?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of the pages where the corrections are made, do you see the date, 1st of April, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Seven years ago actually. Can you tell the name of the signature written there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Three years. I was thinking back further. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be Andreas Manthey.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you sure about the last name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very good at pronouncing Andreas's last name unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember who this person was?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the German investigator that took over the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And you were not present during any corrections to the statement or the read-back to the witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I just observed his initials on there where the corrections were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now going back to 16th of January 2002, when you took the statement at the witness's house, did you follow the same procedures you've outlined to us that you take when you show photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall which photo line-ups you showed this witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: U-1 and U-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When the witness looked at U-1, what did he say or what happened? Did he recognise anybody?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could look at my notes, I would know the exact verbiage, if that's what you would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, that should be on a page 4 of the typewritten statement or on page 10 of your handwritten statement.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: He viewed U-2 and he positively identified Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you record which position that Fatmir was in on have version of U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And as usual did you have the witness circle number 3 and sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The photo sheet?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I would attach it to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about in U-1?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember in U-1 he said that the suspect Isak Musliu looked familiar to him but he could not positively identify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did the witness say the name Isak Musliu? I'm just trying to clarify your answer.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could look at my notes one more time, I would remember. He said number 4, and Isak Musliu was number 4 in that particular line-up but he said he wasn't sure. He said, I can't be for sure. So at which time I had him -- I just placed that in my notes and attached the line-up with the notes also written on the photo line-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if you look at your notes -- well, strike that. Thank you, Mr. Kereakes. I don't have any more questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kereakes. I represent Fatmir Limaj, together with Karim Khan who sits to my right here.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you carefully, first of all, about identification procedures and how experienced you were to be undertaking such a task in this case. Now, first of all, when you were in the United States of America before you went to Kosovo, in particular had you had occasion to deal with photo line-ups as they're called in America?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the procedures, the protocols and the guidelines that existed in Illinois and Chicago in particular at that time, that is, the time before you went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were you particularly aware of the factors that the American courts took into account in relation to assessing the reliability of any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. identification that might occur on a photo line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of the factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, in the light of those answers, what does the Illinois State Code of Criminal Procedure provide with regard to a photo spread?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a pretty general question. I would have to look at the Illinois criminal law and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm just asking you now whether you have any idea what the code said. If you can't remember all the details, that's perfectly understandable, but just some of the protections and some of the guidelines that were in place before you went to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me. These are two different questions. The witness has talked about being familiar with police procedures. Police have their own standards, procedures, training. It's different from what is in the Criminal Code of the court that the court would used. So I -- he's not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Kereakes will be able to explain that, Mr. Nicholls, if that's the position he has. Yes, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kereakes, what were the protections in place practiced by the police in the United States of America prior to you going to Kosovo with regard to photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you what the Chicago police department trained us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the police academy, but as far as other departments in the United States, I'm not sure, but I can tell you how I was trained and how I practiced them as a police officer in Chicago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Well could you do that, then, please.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. We were taught to -- that a photo line-up must be fair and impartial. In other words, all the characteristics must be similar. Like I explained yesterday, if you have a guy with glasses and he's your suspect, make sure that the other five individuals that you're going to use in that photo line-up all have glasses. If the suspect is balding, make sure the other five individuals are balding. You want similar characteristics. If one of the subjects has a goatee, they should all have a goatee. You don't want anything in particular to identify the suspect that the other individuals don't have. You also never want to at all influence the victim/witness viewing the photo line-up by saying, You know, is this -- does number 2 look familiar? Could it be number 3? Or take a look at number 2 again. You want to remain quiet. You want to give the instructions, stand back, give them enough time to look. Once he makes any type of comments like, Yes, it was number 4, or I'm sure it was number 3, that's the suspect. You can record them in your notes. Because being in Kosovo was so hard to always try to find pictures, you know, we used a database of individuals that we had collected at the time there and that's how we made our photo line-up. In the Chicago police department, though, you know, I can go grab six guys off the streets, take their pictures, you know, and use them in a photo line-up. Or I can request pictures from our photo pool there and it could be done. There it was a little more difficult though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is that it? Is that all you were taught in Chicago?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you that if that's really all you were taught, then you were not taught some of the basic fundamental procedures that apply to photographic as well as other line-ups, were you? Or have you forgotten?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is it? Well, I'll come to what the fundamental procedures are because I make the suggestion clear so you know where I'm going now. I suggest that what happened in Kosovo at your hands was a remarkably crude investigative approach to identification in which fundamental principles were violated by you. Now, do you appreciate what I'm putting to you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You may believe what you wish. Do you understand what I'm putting to you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now once you got to Kosovo, you indicated yesterday that you'd been trained at one point, once you joined the investigative unit, by an officer from the RUC, part of the United Kingdom.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, did that officer train you in photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did review them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. What was the training you got in photo line-ups from him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, similar to what I explained to you earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is that all? Just those principles, fair and impartial and the factors you've indicated are -- ensuring that there were similar characteristics in the others in the line-up, and that you don't influence yourself by anything said, the choice that the person may or may not make?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Also too I forgot to add you have each witness victim view the line-up by himself. Not with any other victim/witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. See, once again, I want to suggest if that's all you were taught, then some of the basic principles that apply in the United Kingdom are flouted once you were in Kosovo. Do you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I may have forgot the exact procedures as far as -- I have been gone from investigations for the last three an a half years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. Are you still in the police?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm on a leave of absence with the police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you last work for the police?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2003, October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So after you left Kosovo, you went back to working for the police?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about seven months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And since then you've been on leave of absence?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I don't obviously want to pry into anything personal, but is it to do with health or something else?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I explained yesterday, I was -- accepted a contractor's position with the US State Department working protection in Afghanistan and Israel, not investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, in any of those circumstances since Kosovo, have you had occasion to consider photo line-ups or line-ups of any kind?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Now I want to ask you this question in relation to line-ups: What is the most fundamental thing that someone who is conducting a photo line-up must ensure that the potential witness who is attending the line-up is told before they view the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: To look at each picture and not to make any guesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Can I suggest there is a very fundamental proposition which underlies certainly the law in the United States of America on this issue, and the law in the United Kingdom on this issue, a fundamental principle. And I suggest you don't even know what it is, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not really an appropriate question. He can ask questions about what the witness did, what the witness knows. But not whether the witness -- continues to ask whether the witness appreciates where he's going, appreciates if he understands his assertions. I think he should ask questions about facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think there are refinements of cross-examination technique, Mr. Nicholls. I don't see anything improper in what's being done. It could be, if the witness was one likely to be confused by it, but Mr. Kereakes is able to appreciate I think what is being put to him quite well. Thank you, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to waste time, Mr. Kereakes. I'm going to put to you what the fundamental issue is here.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The one thing that a witness, potential witness - there are others but one fundamental thing that the witness must be told before viewing the line-up - is that the person - not suspect - but that the person who they have seen in a particular situation may or may not be in the line-up they're being shown. Now, have you ever been told that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Article 1075 of the Illinois Code of Criminal Procedure, which I suggest American police officers in Chicago must know if they're practising, it's 1075(b): "Each eyewitness who views a line-up or photo spread shall sign a form containing the following information. The suspect might not be in the line-up." Have you ever heard that before?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard that, but I had never followed, as far as the not including the suspect in the line-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. And I suggest you didn't follow procedures in Kosovo any more than you did in America. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the procedure in Kosovo. And I believe what you're reading also doesn't mean that we have to have the suspect in the line-up. It also means you can have the suspect in the line-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. I think you're not following, Mr. Kereakes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm tracking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The important thing for a potential witness is that they are not influenced in believing that the person who you regard as a suspect is the person who they may have seen and, secondly, that the person who they may have seen is amongst those who they're seeing, particularly if they're only seeing seven faces or six faces. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the second part of this Article: "The eyewitness should not assume that the person administering the line-up or photo spread knows which person is the suspect in the case." Now you yesterday indicated very clearly when you took somebody into a room, in general terms applying it to this case, you would first of all ask them if the suspect was in the line-up. That was the wording you used yesterday. Is that what the wording you used at the time in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to suggest to you, Mr. Kereakes, you haven't got the slightest idea how to conduct an impartial and fair line-up. Have you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now another feature is, of course, that -- I want to ask you about this, is that the -- whatever goes on in a photo line-up should be properly recorded at the time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Dated as to when it happened?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Signed by the witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And this applies to whether there has been an identification, just as much as when there hasn't.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, not a procedure that you followed in this case. Is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I did have them attach the photo line-up to the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We'll come to that. And I want to just -- again, dealing with general principles, since you haven't mentioned them but I'm going to mention them to you to save time. The other thing you have to ensure before you even get a witness to a line-up is that the witness has given as full a description in physical appearance and clothing as possible. You're aware of that, are you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest that's another one you haven't actually encountered in this case. You haven't actually done it in this case, have you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't quite understand the first question you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In this case - we'll come to it, specific instances - you as a matter of procedure you have not ensure that individual witnesses you are dealing with have actually recorded a full description of the person who they say they saw, whether it's in a camp on a hillside or wherever it was. You haven't got them to give a full description in all cases, have you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But you recognise it's particularly important if you're only going to show their faces, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have access to a database of, let's say, a person's clothing. If he was wearing a black UCK uniform which identified the military police of the UCK, I did not have suspects -- or I did not have enough pictures of six people dressed in black uniforms in order for him to say, Yeah, that's the suspect's face, along with the patch, along with the boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, I don't think you're understanding, and it may be, once again, you're a totally inappropriate person to be conducting identifications. May I put it again: If in fact in a photo line-up, which happened in this case, where the person I represent, Fatmir Limaj, all you're asking somebody to look at are faces. Yes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You're going to have to ensure that the person who you're asking to identify has already given you a description as far as they can of the facial characteristics.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see what you're mean. The British English sometimes throws me off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, translation.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now you understand?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In each case I did try to get --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: A description of the height, weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When we get through we'll see that, will we? All right. Because one of the further problems is that you want to ensure, where possible, whether the person who again you're asking to look at the line-up is in fact recognising somebody as opposed to identifying somebody. Now, do you know the distinction between those two?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Recognising and identifying?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the exact definition here with me, but as far as recognising, is this the person that he is familiar with? Whereas the person that he identifies, is this the person that actually was the one that committed the crime against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I suggest once again you're way off beam, if that's an understandable phrase in America.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, right. Well, off the park, off the wall, whatever. I don't want to take up time with phrases. Now, what I want to get to with regard to this is the distinction that is drawn in most jurisdictions with regard to this issue is you want to know whether the person you're asking to look at the line-up knows the person from before. In other words, is recognising somebody they know - maybe a relative, could be a friend, very important in Kosovo - as opposed to identifying somebody they'd never seen before in their lives. Now are you aware of that distinction?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. But when I asked you the question, you didn't seem to remember it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's a matter of understanding - if I could intrude - I thought that was the effect of what the witness said, but maybe I had too generous an approach to the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I make no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So you recognise the significance of ensuring that you find out, first of all - this is before we ever get to the line-up - the extent to which the person is able to say, Well, I knew this person anyway, a member of my family or a distant cousin, as opposed to, Never seen the person before in my life, and the first time he walked through the door that's the first time I saw him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did ask him questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. How did you find out it was Isak Musliu, did you know him before the war? A lot of times the witnesses would say, No, no, he was my neighbour, or we went to school together, or I knew him, I had a confrontation with him before. So I did try to establish if a relationship had existed before the detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you recorded all of that, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on which -- I don't understand which witness you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We'll come to the witnesses. Whereas a matter of course would you record that distinction?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be in a statement or it could even be in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What was the protocol? What was the procedure that you used as a matter of course?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would record it in a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Statement.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: By the witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you ever make a statement about these matters at the time? I don't mean the one in 2003 and the one in 2004, after it was all over. I mean at the time, did you make a witness statement about these processes of identification?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You did?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. So when a witness -- it doesn't matter who he is, A, B or C, when a witness either does or doesn't identify, do you make a statement yourself, under your own name saying, On such-and-such a day I showed a line-up to so and so. He did or he didn't identify in the following circumstances. Did you ever make a statement like that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You did? Because I'll be corrected, we don't have those statements if you did do them.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could show you an example in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's not the notes. It's a statement.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry in the statement. I can show you an example in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. A statement by you at the time.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also have it in my notes too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, sorry, please answer the question. Are there any statements, at the time of these purported lineups in which you state under your name, signed by you and dated by you that the identification procedure has taken place. Are there any such statements?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you have them there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show you in these statements right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, since you wish to do so, could you just indicate -- I don't want any names read out in public session because we're in public session.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I look through them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 3, second page, I believe it's marked 0323-2581, but it's crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, that's just --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the next page 0323-2582, but it's been crossed out. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I put in there reporting -- all the way at the bottom last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Reporting investigator then displayed a photo line-up with suspect Isak Musliu and five other Albanian KPS officers. The above witness positively identified Isak Musliu as one of the suspects in the illegal detention centre. They beat him. Review exhibit U-1."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I will come to these because of course they're important. I suggest -- you do understand what a witness statement is, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. What is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: A witnesses statement is the one that I recorded at the time explaining --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know how to make a witness statement, Mr. Kereakes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know how to make one, yourself, for yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. I will ask the question again. At the time, let us take August 2001 as it happens to be in tab 3, did you make at the time of this investigation a witness statement by you -- are you following?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedures we had in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you just answer the question, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not make a separate witness statement in which the suspect photo line-up that I had conducted in -- which I signed and dated. I -- I put it either in the witness statement or in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We'll come to just how bad the notes were and your difficulties of recollection in 2003, because you've had a lot of difficulty recollecting what happened, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, none at all?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: For anything that counsel has asked me, I have remembered so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So far.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, we'll come to the difficulties. I'm dealing with general principles before you ever get to the line-up. Another fundamental question, I suggest, is to discover whether the person who you're asking to look at the photographic line-up has seen a photograph of this person before. Do you recognise that as a principle? Do you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ask any single witness in this case whether they had, in fact, seen the photograph before?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not taught that or it wasn't required in Kosovo from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, this has a particular relevance to the person that I represent, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And perhaps you could enlighten us as to why it does.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you're saying this is because Mr. Fatmir Limaj is a public figure, which at the time, when I initially heard the name, I did not know who Fatmir Limaj was. I didn't think at that time to ask these questions of the witness or the victim, and it's because I never knew he was such a -- in the public eye at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It didn't take long to find out though, did it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I didn't find out till a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How much later?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Certainly before you started doing photo line-ups which you only compiled much later.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do the photo line-ups. I had requested someone to do them for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, perfectly correct. When you requested someone to do it. By that time you knew perfectly well who Fatmir Limaj was as a person, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know towards the end of the investigation or towards the end -- when I was leaving Kosovo at what -- I knew he was a commander in the UCK, but I didn't know that he had now transformed and gone into a political role.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, you knew full well about the fact that he was a political figure. You made that clear to anybody who you had cause to detain and we'll come to that. You knew who he was and what he looked like, because he's on television. You knee he'd been on television, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. After. Not in the beginning of investigating him I did not know. Even towards the middle of the investigation I knew that he was a commander from UCK. He knew he had some kind of political role, but I did not know the exact, you know, position that he had in the political spectrum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Didn't you? As an investigating officer, I suggest that you must have known and, if you didn't you would have made enquiries to find out who he is and whether his picture appeared in the newspapers and on television. You would want to know that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time I was -- when I started investigating this case, it was more important to start identifying the victims, the witnesses, and also the suspects. But I didn't start going into full depths of who these suspects are as far as what are they doing now. I had asked several questions in the witness statements asking, Where is he now? But I had even requested backgrounds on these individuals from KFOR, from other databases, but I had not sat down actually and began, you know, building up a profile and finding out what exactly are they doing now. I was busy recording the statements or exhuming mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I am much more interested on this score the extent to which you knew that Fatmir Limaj's photograph, his image, his picture was widespread, his name was a household name, I suggest, in the years after the war, and his picture appeared in the press and television regularly. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I did find that out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Later?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just tell us how much later. When was it you say you discovered that.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was more towards the end of the investigation once I started finding out more about him, and it wasn't towards -- I know for sure it was not towards the beginning and even towards the middle of my investigation, I still had not put -- known that he was a political figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you recognise that there is a risk here that if somebody's picture has been all over the press and television that people who then identify line-ups may be identifying the person they've seen on television or in the press. You recognise that risk, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That is why, I suggest, as an investigating officer, you have to be extremely careful to ensure that you have discovered that information before you even attempt to line-up. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be important for me to know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the investigation and now that I'm thinking back on it. But at the time, if you're new to Kosovo, as an investigator, and, you know, somebody comes in, reports a war crime and gives you the name Fatmir Limaj, and you don't know that name, you just continue your investigation, recording statements, gathering evidence. I did not know at the time that he had been in newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm still on the preparatory stage before you ever show photographs. The one thing, another fundamental thing you would need to discover from your potential witness, having gone through these preliminaries, most of which, I suggest, in your case, you haven't done, but once you've gone through the preliminaries, what's the final question you must ask the witness before you even take them into the room where the line-up is?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the final question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It would help to know, wouldn't it, whether the witness says he or she is able to recognise or identify, using those terms carefully, the person that they saw again, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did ask them that though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You recognise it is important?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. And I did ask him that. I didn't know there was going to be the final question per procedure to say, As soon as I'm going to take you in this room, the final question I have to ask you is: Can you still recognise this suspect. The way you're putting it is you're saying that we have a check-list, and on that check-list first question is, you know, Have you seen this guy in the media. Second question is, Have you seen him in the newspapers. No such check-list existed at CCIU or I could say in any particular police department. And finally, there isn't, you know, the last final question before you go in there, you know, Can you identify. I've already established that I believe before I have shown the suspect --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, have you now?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So we'll find that on statements, will we, the few records that we have, that you asking the question and the response, will we?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. I suggest once again, Mr. Kereakes, you're completely wrong. It does not occur on the documents we have and we'll go through them, don't worry. Now, in relation to the line-up itself that is assembling the photographs, you got someone else to do it from a database. What's the minimum number in the United States of America or let us put it more precisely, in Chicago, that are required? The minimum number.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least six.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: At least six. And you would recognise yourself, would you not, that in fairness six is the minimum but it is really much better to have more, if you can.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ask in this case whether you could have or find more than six in these cases?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At one point I did and we had trouble finding similar characteristics. Our database was small. We just didn't have enough pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you just turn to the one we have in the bundle that you've been provided with, tab 2.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bundle?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you got tab 2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the photograph number 2 doesn't provide a very similar appearance, does it, on that line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You think it does. In terms of hair, did anyone describe the person who they purported to say was Fatmir Limaj with hair like that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: With brown hair?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dark hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How can you tell that's brown hair?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell it's dark hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Now, please be careful. Did any witness that you can recall, dealing with the question of purporting to identify Fatmir Limaj, ever describe the person they saw and thought was Fatmir Limaj with hair of that length?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the hair in each photo is very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You think the hair in these six photographs are very similar, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 is a little bit longer but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: A little bit longer. Mr. Kereakes, how much care and attention have you paid to this case?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, really?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I was working it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in relation to these six, just -- I'm just looking at tab 2 still, these six, one of them, of course, appears on these photographs to have facial hair; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it. Maybe you have a better copy than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would like to know which one he's referring to as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was just wondering you're saying has facial hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, it appears on the photocopies, and I will come to the originals in a moment, number 4 appears to have facial hair.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to me that it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It doesn't? Well, in order to resolve these, did you ensure that the originals of any photographs that were going to be shown were preserved so we could tell?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The originals were taken from a database.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So what was being shown in a photo line-up were photocopies of a copy. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, I suggest, not entirely satisfactory, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're in Kosovo working it is pretty satisfactory, considering the fact that we did not have a photo department to make the pictures nice and clear, be able to make duplicate pictures at all time. We just did not have access to that type of technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: There's an Albanian community in the United States of America, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was any request made by you of the American authorities to be provided with a much bigger database from America?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also asked my commander several times to get us better type of photo equipment and along with Albanian-American language assistance, or other nationalities that spoke fluent Albanian, and I never got any of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was the supervisor Dennis Sherman?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why did you stop being a part of the investigation unit in February 2002?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I transferred to another department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or were you moved?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not moved. I transferred to another department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you have a disagreement with the very man we've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did have a difference of opinion with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. And were you moved because it was recognised that you were not up to the job?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. I received a great letter of commendation from him. I was also promoted to a chief of investigation position for a task force for the police commissioner, and I even received invitations to join the regional murder squad, which I did later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What was the disagreement about?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- had to do with another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Nothing to do with this case?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to move in general terms from assembling the line-up to be shown to the showing of a line-up. I've already dealt with one of the aspects of the showing, which is indicating that -- to the witness that the person they've seen, as opposed to the suspect, may or may not be present. And I want to move to another factor. Did you indicate to any of the witnesses the standard of certainty that had to be reached before they picked out a photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what did you say the standard was?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't want him to guess. You know, I wanted him to be 100, positively, sure that when he picked the person in that line-up that that was the person that committed the crimes against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So you wanted the person to be sure?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you told them that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And that's recorded?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. That's recorded, is it, that that's what you've told them. I've been asking you about records being kept of the whole procedure so we knew what questions were asked, so we know what the witness was told. That was recorded, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered, no, that's what I told him verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Why don't you record it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't required of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In relation to the viewing itself, did you record how long the actual exercise took?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we didn't record it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You do recognise that it may have a bearing on the reliability, the reliability of any identification as to how long it took, how much care was taken, how many times particular photographs were looked at, whether other photographs were hesitated over. That kind of thing. You do appreciate all of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yeah, right. Did you record any of that on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recorded when a statement began and when a statement ended, if I did finish the -- if I did show the photo line-up I would have placed that in the witness statement as far as what time the whole statement ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's a very different matter.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see some of the factors taken into account in America -- I mean you've been to court in America over identifications, have you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In Illinois?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So you know the kind of things that the court is looking towards in assessing on reliability, do you, in America?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And can I just read you the factors to see if you agree that these are the factors, at least in America, that are relevant to the reliability of a line-up. The witnesses opportunity to view the suspect at the time of the crime is where it starts. You're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The witness's degree of attention, you're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The accuracy of the witness's prior description of the suspect?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The level of certainty demonstrated at the time of the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The length of time between the crime and the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In this case, quite considerable.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And any acquaintance with the suspect prior to the crime.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You're aware of all of those factors?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I suggest I've taken a little time to take you through the general principles and I now want to deal with some specific instances with you. For the moment, I can certainly do it in public session without referring to the name of the person who we're concerned with. If you turn to tab 4, there is a particular witness mentioned there. Now, that is also -- or that person is also somebody you referred to in tab 3 in your supplement continuation form notes. And that's Appendix A. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. I'm just going to, for the moment, call this, if I may, this person A. Can I just call him A, so that there is no risk of... So when you first were involved in this -- in this investigation, you viewed this witness as a central witness, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you were given, to start off with, a record of an interview that had been had with him. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I'm using your words. You were impressed by the account that you read of that interview, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You thought it was graphic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought the statement in itself was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the first question I have on this: Did you have anything to do with taking that statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the first statement that -- when I was first assigned the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: On witness A?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. The interview. So it is clear, this was an interview that had taken place on the 20th of August, 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me which one you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to come to it. Don't worry --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just wanted to tell the witness who is looking that it is not in the binder in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It is not in that bundle. But I want to ask you about it, and I'm going to let you see it in a minute, if you need to. Did you have anything to do with an interview of this witness we're calling A for these purposes in public, on the 20th of August 2000?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. On the 20th of August, 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a little bit confused because I know that I wasn't working for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. CCIU on the 20th of August 2000, so I'm not sure if you're referring to the statement that was taken by investigator Kaare Birkeland or the statement that was taken of witness A, by myself or I think unless you have the dates wrong. 20th of August 2002 I had arrived at Kosovo and I wasn't working for CCIU.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see it's a fairly minor matter but I suggest even on minor matters you are all over the place. You made a statement or rather you were interviewed and it resulted in a statement in 2004, September and November of 2004. Do you remember? It was last year.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Again, I will show you the document if you wish to see it. I want to, if I can, do it without necessarily belaboring you with documents. And in paragraph 3 of that interview statement with you last year, you said, you interviewed A, the witness we're calling A, on the 20th of August 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the Prosecution told you that there was a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh. Well, --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it should be 2001. It would be easier if I could see the statement you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Because in fact it can't be a typo, do you follow? And you're welcome to add any explanation you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could we have -- I don't know whether it is available -- a record of the interview. I can give the page, it's 84015. Is there a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The witness has that. That's in your hard bound binder, marked 2004, the witness statement, if that's the one Mr. Mansfield is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but this is not the statement I took. This is the one, like I said, was taken by Kaare Birkeland, so that would mean I'm not all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. We're slightly at cross-purposes. I want you to look at your interview statement, in view of your answers --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe instead of saying "your interview statement," which could also mean statements taken by the witness, counsel could say the witness statement which you provided to ICTY, make it a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This is a statement you provided to the ICTY last year. It's got two dates on it which you say you remember, September 2004 and November 2004. We've certainly been provided with supplemental information about this statement that there is an error in this paragraph, but I want to ask you how the error occurred in the first place. Now, do you have a copy in front of you now of the statement you provided to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could tell the witness there were two ICTY witness statements in there. The one Mr. Mansfield was referring to should be labelled 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. If you would look at -- first of all, just so it is clear, you will see on the first sheet or should be on the first sheet, dates I've been mentioning, which they're regarded as an interview but it obviously results in a statement you provide. You see the dates 24th of September, 2004 and the 10th of November, 2004. You see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, if you turn over the page, I'm dealing with a particular point at this stage, paragraph 3: "I am providing this statement at the request of the ICTY to clarify a few matters in my investigation. I interviewed," then I will insert A "on the 20th of August, 2000," with a reference to page numbers, "and again on the 17th of August, 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's not a typo, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How does that typo come about?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, on witness A, where it says I interviewed him on the 20th of August, 2000, that's a mistake. I believe I arrived in Kosovo on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. How does a statement, in your name, because I'm going to suggest you are thoroughly careless with dates, times even those relating to yourself, and this is an example. How does that get into the statement which presumably you then sign? Don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see on the first page, I was assigned in Afghanistan, and the interview took place over the phone and also via e-mail. I didn't have any access to any of the case files that were with me. I printed it up, and I remember that I was trying to remember the exact dates and I read through the statement, I signed it, but I did not catch that error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, it's a fairly major error, because according to you, you weren't even on the job in August 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, we're dealing here -- I didn't preface all of this, this is minor. We'll get to major matters in a moment. This is a minor matter. Now I'm still dealing with this witness who I am calling A for the moment. I think you should have what is referred to there in that statement as the interview or statement of A on the 20th of August, 2000. You should have a copy. And it is 03230787 in your bundle of statements.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He does not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have one that was handed to me a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't realise you handled it. You said the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, just to make sure, I will go slowly. This is witness A. We're calling him A for the moment, and it is the 20th of August, 2000. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this -- first of all, the person who actually did the interviewing of this person on the 20th of August, 2000, is that person's name on the statement anywhere? I don't mean the name of the witness, the name of the person doing the investigation or interviewing.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So how do you know who took it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing else attached to this when it was given over?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I pause for a moment to check. I have a bundle. As far as I'm aware, that's the only other thing that came with it, that particular one. Am I right? Yes. That's the only thing we've been provided with. Anyway, from that document - I won't take up a load of time - there is no way of knowing, it would appear, on the face of the document, who actually took this one in August 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. Now when you read it and you were impressed by it, was there something that later was rather obvious to you about this statement? No?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with Fatmir Limaj, shall we, whom I represent.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you recognise or realise that in this initial statement he's not mentioned at all? Is he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I take a quick glance at this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. You're very welcome to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield, the witness is needing to look through the statement carefully. Given the clock, I think we might leave your question or the answer to it until after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kereakes, you've had an opportunity to look at the interview or statement by this witness A made in August 2000, and do you agree that that statement does not mention Fatmir Limaj or the name Celiku, does it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to deal carefully with how things progress over this witness. You see this witness A - and so it's clear, we can follow it in tab 3, you have before you, tab 3 - on the 17th of August 2001, so it's a year later?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And on this page of a supplementary continuation form, you have in fact a list of suspects numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. And I want to ask you, carefully, if you can help us as to how the name Fatmir Limaj came up at all a year later, it never having been mentioned before by this witness.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go to tab 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I can understand in tab 4 we have the witness's statement and we can see the one that you took on the 17th of August, and there's a paragraph on page 0794 where Fatmir Limaj, Celiku, is mentioned as the commander of the area. All right?
