utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to tread carefully because some of this, what is said here, so you understand, actually hasn't been said by this witness in his evidence. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what I'm interested in, for the present, is how the name "Fatmir Limaj" came to be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness told me that in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you mention the name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you ask him whether, in fact, he knew somebody called Fatmir Limaj and that's how it came up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even know who Fatmir Limaj was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I know, you said that before. Were you aware that in the year 2000, that's the year before you arrived, and in the year 2001 Fatmir Limaj had been standing in local elections in the year 2000 for mayor of Pristina and his photograph was all offer the city and as a member of the Assembly in the summer of 2001 at the very time you're there with his photograph all over the city. You did know that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No? Why do you think that's funny?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because before I even went to Kosovo, I didn't even know where Yugoslavia was. So I knew nothing of the politics. I didn't know anything of the political figures. Or when I even got there, I was assigned to the Kosovo Polje police station, which is outside of Pristina, and I didn't know anything to do any of the politicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, as a street police officer you walk around with your eyes shut, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Not on my beat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you saying you didn't see a single poster with this man's name and photograph up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw many posters while I was there, but I didn't pay attention to the names or to who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or did this witness, in fact not know the name Fatmir Limaj at that time that you were speaking to him and he knew the name Celiku? Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not. Because how he told me the name is how I wrote it in the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I'm trying to get at is whether this witness has been subjected to heavy suggestion from you.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, let's just look at the statement, since you said look at the statement, 03230794, the paragraph which begins "the commander of the whole area was." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. What's written above it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: "He beat me on two separate occasions. Always I was handcuffed and he used his hands and feet on me."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I think we may be looking at the wrong passage. Because witness A, 0794 --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right? I'm looking at the paragraph. The commander -- I'm only dealing with Fatmir Limaj and how the name came up. "The commander of the whole area was Fatmir Limaj." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's halfway down.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, above that sentence, something is written.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I know -- oh, you mean the little handwritten notes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I know only Celiku. Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Whose writing is that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be Andreas or Edgar's.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's not your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. And it appears that that has been added in handwriting therefore, if you look at 0796, that this was a statement that was amended in 2002 on the 3rd of the 4th 2002, nine months later. Do you see that, at the end?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So it looks as though the handwritten additions not in your writing but in the writing of the person dealing with him after you'd finished, you'd gone from this investigation --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: -- yes? Has written "at that time I knew him only as Celiku".

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, let's just think about this. If he only knew him as Celiku at that time, how is he able to say his name was Fatmir Limaj to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's completely misleading, confusing way of reading it. "At that time" he's correcting his statement, at that time refers to 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hadn't understood it to be anything else, Mr. Nicholls. And I don't think Mr. Mansfield suggested anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's right. I'm not suggesting that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Can you help, Mr. Kereakes, about this matter?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would have to agree with the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You don't have to, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, what I believe -- sometimes when taking statements, you know, the witnesses would throw certain things out there, Oh, by the way so you know the commander of that area is Fatmir Limaj Celiku. I believe what Andreas or Edgar, because I'm not sure who, I believe this is Andreas, what he did here was, he's saying at the time of the detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry, I can't -- that's all I could offer. But I know that if I wrote in there "the commander of the whole area was Fatmir Limaj, Celiku," that's something that the witness A would have thrown out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Because, you see, I appreciate my learned friend's interjection about the date of it. Of course I appreciate it's referring to the time. See, what you say here is -- or rather what the witness is telling you, is that he learnt the name at the time, that is his name. If you look at the later sentence, "from other prisoners I learnt his name and that he was the commander of the whole area." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure where you're at right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In the same paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just a couple of sentences further on.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: "From other prisoners I learned his name." Well, what name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he's referring to Fatmir Limaj, Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Both names?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my writing it would be Fatmir Limaj, Celiku, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, quite. But then apparently according to the writing that is written on later, he didn't know the name Fatmir Limaj in 1998. He only knew the name Celiku in 1998.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible. But he was clarifying to me that at that time, when I was taking the statement, that the commander of the whole area was Fatmir Limaj, Celiku. He had already put them together, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, did you --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: (redacted), you know, I had learned the name from other prisoners as this was Celiku. But when I was taking the statement from him, you know, he turned and he said the commander of the region at that time was, and he gave his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How did he know the full name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was two years later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How did he know the full name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had probably either asked people about it, found out from other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or did you suggest the name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know who Fatmir Limaj was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, yes you did, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: He was one of the main suspects you were being asked to investigate, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, at the time I took this statement is when I first started with CCIU. I did not know Fatmir Limaj, Celiku. I did not know any of these suspects at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I just want to continue on this theme of the name for the moment. Did you ask this witness why he hadn't mentioned -- now whether it's Celiku or Fatmir Limaj -- or these two instances that he puts in this statement, why he hadn't mentioned this before in the previous statement in 2000?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I review my statement real quick?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of questions I had for this particular witness after I read the initial statement by Investigator Birkeland. And once he started talking, I just documented exactly what he was telling me, and I didn't catch it at first, that this name hadn't been mentioned in the first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, you wouldn't take long to discover, would you, as an investigator, if it's being done this way, that, in fact, having read and been impressed by his August 2000 statement, that none of this is mentioned in that statement. The one question to test the veracity of your witness is to ask him why he's never mentioned it before. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Can we go into private one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I won't take up time. I asked you why you hadn't asked the obvious question as to why it hadn't been asked before, and you answered in short form is that you didn't think it was significant. Now I just want to continue, again dealing with this witness who we're calling A for these purposes. Having -- this witness having mentioned the commander of the area, it would be important for you to see if this person was capable of identifying him, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. And that's what you did in one form or another, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, no. On this occasion.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I identified him through the name, but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The question is: Having brought the name up for the first time, can he actually identify the person he says he's seen twice? Actually look at the pictures and identify him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not have pictures at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you -- you didn't have any pictures of Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But you did of others?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see in the -- in my sub report on the first time, is I had a picture of Isak Musliu, and the reason for that was because he had been mentioned in the first statement. (redacted) (redacted), so I didn't have a photo line-up established yet, which for me to show at that time the witness, witness A, the suspect photo line-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So when was the photo line-up U-2, in relation to Fatmir Limaj, assembled by somebody who you had asked to do it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Please help us. We're only dealing with about a year that you're actually involved in all of this. This interview is in August, 2001. How long after that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I begin looking through a -- my sup report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that is being done, there will be another redaction of the name that was just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My supplemental log which shows the actions to be taken, which says "must identify and create photo line-up for the suspect," I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. Well, I will leave that for the moment.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you personally, once the line-up was in your possession, show it to this witness A?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness A was never shown Fatmir Limaj by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look in my notes, but I believe I wasn't the one who showed him that picture. I'm almost sure that I didn't. Didn't show him that, the photo line-up. I had requested that one be created, but I don't -- I don't believe I had another chance to interview him again in order to show the picture, because then he had entered the protective custody and I had not -- I believe I didn't have the photo line-up yet done, or -- I know I -- it wasn't me that showed it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, in view of those answers, I would like you to see - and you have it in front of you - another statement that you provided to this Tribunal, for the purposes of this Tribunal, dated 2003. Would you kindly look at that. You have it in a separate bundle, I think, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You might cross-check it. I think you have it separately detailed there. The one from 2003 which has paragraph numbers in it.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you kindly look at paragraph 96. I'm going to take it slowly and carefully to avoid mentioning, again, names in public. Have you got paragraph 96?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In this paragraph, vis-a-vis witness A, you say this: "I cannot recall how many witnesses that I personally showed the suspect sheets to, but I do recall showing A," - I leave out the rest - "photographs of Fatmir Limaj." And then in the next paragraph you say: "I recall that A identified Limaj." I leave out the other names. Do you see all that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's complete nonsense, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a mistake and I can explain what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. How did the mistake happen?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the ICTY investigators came out to Chicago to interview me, I didn't have my continuation of my sub report with me, so I can refer. I could have sworn that I had shown the picture of Fatmir, but I had made the mistake without looking at my notes and signed that. I shouldn't have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, I suggest, if you are right that it's a mistake, it's a pretty serious mistake for you to be making and signing a statement as a police officer, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I'm not proud of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: On the other hand, of course, you're pretty sure that you did show a photograph of Fatmir Limaj to witness A, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just testified that I don't believe I showed a picture. In order for me to confirm that I'd have to see my supplemental continuation, but I'm almost sure that I had made that mistake about concerning Fatmir Limaj to witness A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, what the wording of -- you can see it on the screen, the wording you just told the Tribunal is "I could have sworn that I'd shown the picture of Fatmir." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's what I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I went through my supplement continuation report and I looked at it, I saw that, yeah, I had created the suspect photo, I had requested it to be created, I had shown it to a couple of other witnesses, and I couldn't remember -- and I had assumed that, well, witness A, was my first witness. I remember showing him the one photo line-up and I had gotten so routine into showing both suspect photo line-ups to future witnesses I had made the mistake and said, U-2, which was the suspect, I had shown it also to him. And that was a mistake on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you notice the mistake?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed the mistake when I came here and I had time to look through all my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So in March of this year?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I'm -- oh, yes, in March of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: March of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour perhaps we should go into private session, just for the next two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Can I just summarise in public session in relation to a third name, who for these purposes we will just call C, in a statement that you made, you showed him photographs of Fatmir Limaj when he hadn't even mentioned the person, is that right, that's the summary?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some further questions about some other individuals. And I want to do it in public as far as possible without mentioning names, so if you could be careful --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: -- and I will do the same. If you look behind tab 5 - you dealt with this this morning - there is another statement by an individual who is named there. Tab 5, please.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, first of all, did you ask this witness -- I will call him tab 5 witness so it is clear on the record. Did you go through all the formalities with this witness, tab 5? The questions that I've put in the past; you know, have you seen him before, can you give me a good description, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statement, he knew him. He mentioned him in a statement that he was his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. But of course, even if somebody says that, it's important to get a description from the person who says he knows him, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Because a person's appearance may change?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it may.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Especially in wartime, if that's what was going on at that time, people may grow beards, they may not have beards, they may have moustaches, they may have very short hair, very long hair, all of that kind of thing. On a face identification matters, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Where are the questions?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, he said he was his commander so he knew him, so I didn't ask that question. He was under his command. He had taken orders from him, so he said he did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you following the question?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So why didn't you ask him, somebody who claimed to know him, why didn't you ask him some of the basic questions?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, looking at my statement, I did ask about the other two suspects in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, please stick to Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what I did, I forgot to ask -- get a physical description from him concerning --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You forgot?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I'm going to suggest that's not all if what happens in this case, that is tab 5 witness, would you turn to the second page, 1051. Now, all that the statement indicates here is that you showed a photo line-up marked U-2 and that the witness identified number 3. All right? That's what the statement -- your statement says.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry, to be more precise, the statement that is taken from tab 5 witness. Now, the first question is: What happened to the U-2 line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying what I do with the line-up afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is I attach it to the statement -- or first I have the witness circle it, circle the number, sign it, then I would attach it to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. You're sure?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you been asked yourself, when you got here, about where it might be?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You appreciate that it's not available now, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Bad use of English as opposed to American. You understand that it's not available.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sure you don't appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, right. I understand what you mean. Are you aware that when another set of officers took over the investigation from you and still later the whole investigation was handed over -- you know that's what happened?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You know that much. No one, no one has ever found a version of the U-2 line-up in which Fatmir Limaj appears at position 3. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I could think of is, you know, this -- this case had been copied and maybe that that piece of paper was lost. That's the only explanation I have. I know if I had written in my notes that I displayed them and he identified them as number 3, it was always my procedure to then inventory it with the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, you would be stapling the photo line-up to the English version or the Albanian version?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually I would use a paper clip and I would put -- I would either staple or paper clip and I would put the Albanian version, the English version, and the photo line-up together in a binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were they stapled?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I stapled. Sometimes I used paper clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Because if they were stapled, the originals would have the staple marks, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Hmm. Have you looked at the originals?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original statement or -- the original witness statement or the original suspect photo line-up?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Both, actually.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, because the original -- no I haven't seen originals. I've just been handed copies. But at one time I had seen the originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, all right. See, so it's clear again where I'm going, this isn't the only instance of this. We'll come to another one where it just doesn't seem to be in existence anymore. You can't help about this at all, is that the position?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish I could. I know that they were there. I wouldn't have -- I wouldn't have created a suspect photo line-up and per the directions of the Prosecutor at the time he had us circle the number of the -- had the witness circle the number of the suspect, sign it, and then we would inventory it along with the -- with the original witness report. And the translated copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, looking at the witness's statement, tab 5 witness, has this tab 5 witness actually -- as opposed to yourself and another witness -- has he signed or initialled this statement, either the English version or the Albanian version which you have attached to it in this copy?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a signature on the back page of 0323-1054, but I was not present for this signing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So on 1054, you're pointing, are you, to the -- an apparent signature in the top left-hand corner, is that it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure whose that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: See, looking -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I could assist counsel, the same signature appears on 1052 in the place which appears to be signature in the declaration, if one looks at the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The signature, if that is the signature of the witness, I think what you just said was, you're not present when the statement is signed.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So when is it signed by the witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once we have it translated from English to Albanian, he's then called in to come in and sign the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, that's -- that particular witness, I want to give you another example, which is tab 6, please.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Again I'm going to call it, this one, the tab 6 witness. It will take a little longer. Now, the tab 6 witness gives a relatively lengthy statement, as you can see. And in the statement, in describing things that happened, he does not mention the name Fatmir Limaj in the body of the statement. Does he? Check it if you wish.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, I'm going to ask you how this witness managed to come up with the name. If you look at 1251 - your attention was directed to this earlier on - there is the passage where a photo line-up apparently relating to Limaj was shown to him.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I just want to take out -- take you to the sentences before we get to that. Do you see the question which is apparently from you: "How did you figure out the commander Celiku was Fatmir Limaj?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, if you look -- if you keep your finger in that page and turn to 1261, is that question I've just posed to you "how did you figure out the commander Celiku," do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is that your writing?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, this is a question, in your writing, posed therefore on the date of this statement, was it, in January 2002?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You certainly knew about Fatmir Limaj by then, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Where on earth in this statement or anywhere does he say prior to this question that he has figured out that Celiku is Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I take a second to review the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at 0323-1250 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he mentions Celiku in the statement, at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry, on 1251 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Should I read for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "As we were walking along, we came to a crossroad where a car pulled up. In this white car a person exit and walks towards us. I described that person as dressed in a green uniform with a pistol at his side, broad face, brown hair, was not wearing" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am asked to ask you if you wouldn't mind slowing down because --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's being translated. I think we're all following the passage on 1250. Yes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard him tell Shala to tell prisoners to sit down. This is how I found out he was a commander. The commander told Shala at this time. I still did not know this UCK commander's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. Let's just pause there. When you were taking this statement in February -- I'm so sorry, January 2002, he told you that whoever the person was, a commander at that stage, and of course there is more than one commander in this whole business, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So it could be anybody, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be either the commander of the prison, it could be the commander of the region, or it could be the commander of the UCK police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, so it could be anybody.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And he's telling you, "at this time." What did you understand him to mean by "this time"?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning at the -- during his detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. "I still do not know this UCK commander's name". I suggest he's telling you that he still didn't know the name of the commander.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, no. That's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning at this time, when the action -- look at the action before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've got a guy giving orders, right? And he's saying "at this time." This time. Not meaning present tense when I'm taking the statement. He's describing something that happened to him -- I'm sorry, I'm going too fast but -- he's describing something that happened to him at the detention centre. We're not talking about what he was doing in his house at that particular moment. We're talking present tense. He said, At that time --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But it doesn't say that, you see. It says "at this time, not "at that time."

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mine says: "At this time I still do not know this UCK commander's name."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, right. Well, for these purposes, it doesn't matter whether it's referring to 1998 or referring to the time of the statement. Where does he tell you that this person who's a commander, one was Celiku and two was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I asked him the question at the end of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Quite. I think you have the point, do you, Mr. Kereakes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like you to -- I would like to explain that a little more, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Certainly. I will allow you to do so, certainly. I don't want to cut you off. What has happened here, you will see on this page, is that the sentence, or part sentence - I think it is a whole sentence - "at this time I still do not know this UCK's commander's name," has been crossed out. Did you cross it out?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what appears - I hope you will follow me here - is that when this statement is checked over later on in 2002 by another officer whose initial is M, 1402, he crosses that out and he writes in "Fatmir Limaj" in the margin and signs it. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So none of that, that's the crossing out and the name, Fatmir Limaj, in the margin, would have been there in January 2002, would it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. So in the body of the statement, as I was putting to you, there is no indication of the name Fatmir Limaj, nor the name Celiku, being the same as Fatmir Limaj, at least on that page, when you took it in January. Let's turn over. 1251, a separate incident right at the end, there was a piece of paper, and there was a commander's signature, he claimed on it, with the name Celiku. Now, that too is not a paragraph in which he says, Celiku was the commander who I'd seen earlier on and is the commander known as Limaj. Is there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. So how did you know, before you worked -- you came to the question -- how did you know that he had figured out that commander Celiku was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a name Celiku on a piece of paper, he said that there was a commander earlier. So I asked him the question and how he had figured it was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Kereakes. These are very simple questions.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, just answer the question, then you can explain. How, how was it that you had thought that he had figured out that Commander Celiku was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe what happened is, when you're translating from Albanian to German, and then German to English, the question that I asked or when I was writing it down, that a lot of it was lost, could have been lost in the translation. So that's what I believed, that while I was trying to clarify, you know, how was this commander -- how did you find out who it was, you know, and what had happened is, part of it could have been lost in the translation, and what I was trying to show at the time was, You had received the name Celiku and there was a commander earlier, how did you figure out that it was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where is your record, in English, of all of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And if we read that, the record in English does not suggest typed or written, that any such questions were asked which might explain it in the way you suggest. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Why not?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that could have been a mistake on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Another one?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just how many mistakes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, when you're translating from a different language --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it's possible that a lot of it was lost in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry. Nothing to do with lost in translation. Do you follow me? This is to do with the questions you ask in English that have to be translated, you write them down so there is a record of how often did you see him, what were the circumstances, what's the full description, have you seen him before, are you able to recognise, how did you work out, all of that. You know, very simple questions. Where is that record in English?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that one question that was sufficient enough to show that he had identified Celiku, who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or is it a case that you were desperate to get Fatmir Limaj identified at all costs?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't desperate to get anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, no?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I want to pause for a moment and ask you about that. Do you know somebody called Gani Imeri [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, at one point the witness wanted to explain about a line being crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And Mr. Mansfield said he was going to let him come back to that. I don't know if we're moving on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I was because there's a supplementary statement, but I will do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Before we pass on to that name I've just put to you, can you explain, therefore, the line that's been crossed out, the name Fatmir Limaj added later, the explanation for your question about how he had worked out that Celiku was Limaj. What's the explanation you wish to give?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why they crossed it out is maybe they're assuming that there was a mistake in there, why the other detectives, the future detectives, crossed that line. I don't know why they did that. At that time, when I wrote -- let me go back to that. When I wrote what the witness had stated "at this time I still did not know the UCK commander's name," meaning at the time of the incident. That's what I wanted to explain. He didn't know the commander's name. He had given the piece of paper with Celiku on, right there and, you know, it was an oversight on my part. How did you figure out -- or how did you figure out that Commander Celiku was Fatmir Limaj. He's saying, In the prison I heard the name Celiku and other prisoners mentioned that it was Fatmir Limaj. If he had heard the name Fatmir Limaj in prison, right, and then later he is given a sheet of paper that says Celiku on it, you know he had already heard of different prisoners who it was or had heard that name, it's reasonable to think he would put them together. He is given a sheet of paper from him saying Celiku on it, and later he remembered, you know, that it was Fatmir Limaj. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It would have been so straightforward, if that's the explanation, for him to have said, on page 1250, At the time I didn't know it, but I learned the name from other prisoners, and it was Commander Celiku or Fatmir Limaj who came up. It would have been so simple, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And he didn't.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But he still continued telling history about that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, At this time I still do not know this UCK commander's name. Meaning at this time, during the incident, during the chain of events he did not know. But then, you know, a little bit later he is given a piece of paper that says Celiku on there, and he had also stated in there he had heard people's name mentioned that, that was Fatmir Limaj, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's only telling you after you put the question, how did you figure out. It's only after that he gives you a description that he claims that he'd heard the name Celiku and other people saying it was Fatmir Limaj in the prison. It's only then?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you, I hope clearly, that you were desperate to get Fatmir Limaj identified and you don't agree.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not desperate to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. That's why I wanted to ask you about a name Gani Imeri. You do remember that name?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. He was detained by you and others for a considerable period of time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. Now when you say by "you and others," are you meaning that CCIU kept them in some office locked up? No, it was by the court after the arrest was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was he charged?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Charges were brought against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were they proceeded with?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they were proceeded with and then later dropped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Dropped? He was in detention for a considerable period of time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the amount of time exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In very difficult circumstances. Wasn't he? Physical circumstances.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the condition of the gaols, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. No heating. No hot shower for six months. All meals are eaten in darkness. The light in his cell turned off. Did you know about any of this?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I wasn't ever visiting the detention centres where they were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But you did have occasion to speak to him from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I saw him once after, in an interview room, at which time he said that he wanted to give the names of the others that were involved in the kidnappings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, right. Now we're getting close to it. I want to -- I'm not able to -- well, I'm able to suggest that -- or I want to ask, first of all, is there any other American or a person wearing an American uniform in Kosovo who had a Greek name involved in all of this? CCIU, I mean obviously.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Because that's the description. And did you on one occasion go and visit this person with an Austrian officer, police officer?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to see my notes on this. I know that a interview was conducted after the arrest, but I'm not sure at that time frame of -- did I go see him. I believe I saw him one more time, but I don't can't remember if I did or not, or was that the initial interview after he was placed under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, later.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, on that later would be -- as soon as he was placed under arrest I know that I conducted an interview in Mitrovica with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I want to suggest to you is that during that interview, you were anxious to get a statement from him which named Fatmir Limaj and that you were indicating to him that if he cooperated, all sorts of privileges, as opposed to detention, might be offered to him, a change of identity, a new location for his family, and so forth. Do you remember all of that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. I remember that, on that particular case -- because it was a different region than Fatmir Limaj's area of responsibility. And I do recall that we did offer him to enter the witness protection programme if he was willing to testify on any other type of war crimes or if any other suspects in the case, that it would all be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, I think just to remind you, he was a commander in the KLA of a battalion in Brigade 141. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. But I believe he became a commander after the newly formed -- from the KLA when it went to the TMK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right? But I believe during conflict that he wasn't a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, what you wanted from him, do you agree, is information and so forth which may become evidence about Fatmir Limaj, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you say his name never came up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you keep notes of the interviews with him, this particular individual?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or it would be in a statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It would be in a statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So on your account, he was offered what you call witness protection, was he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning the case he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me he was scared to give up the names of the other suspects that were involved in the kidnapping of the Serbs and we said at this time that we could offer him protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I suggest all of that was happening in the context of Fatmir Limaj, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I just want to ask you about some other names in the same context. Did you ask him about Hasim Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked him if he was -- if knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So but not Limaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Not asked at all?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Selimi?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He brought up the name Hashim Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In the end, I suggest, this particular witness was offered removal to anywhere in the world if he wanted it, provided he came up with material about Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what has happened in this case -- can I just summarise, it as far as you're concerned -- is you're a police officer from America whose main experience has been inside a housing estate, street crime. Suddenly you find yourself dealing with war crimes. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And you were out of your depth, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't believe I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And nobody was really supervising what you were doing, were they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: International Prosecutor would guide me on a case, would also like Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. look at the case, would want certain things done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If that's the case, I just ask you this: Did the International Prosecutor, whoever it was, ever point out to you that in fact your methods and your approach to identification was seriously flawed?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: On no occasion?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm Gregor Guy-Smith with Mr. Richard Harvey here. I represent Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think we will understand each other. I come from San Francisco.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still may not understand the California.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's see how we do here, all right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's try it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first became involved in police work, you were, at what university?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Loyola University.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know of a place in that area called Northwestern?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where is that? Is that close to where you were?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say it's about, let's see, Loyola is in Rogers Park and Evanston is on -- Northwestern is in Evanston, maybe five miles. Five miles north.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Northwestern, did you ever have any dealings with the centre that they have there, the law school on wrongful convictions?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were getting your training as a police officer, did that issue ever come up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wrongful convictions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my arrests?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. Just generally, as a topic of something that you needed to be concerned about as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the police academy?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before you got involved at the police academy, you also were taking courses in psychology; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what's psychology, the study of the mind?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in that particular field, you learned about various factors that could influence the way an individual would act; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't taking anything related to any type of criminal applied psychology or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But it's one of the things you learned about in psychology.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had just started my Psych 101 class. I just started the major, so I hadn't really gotten that deep into how, you know, certain aspects of psychology can get into -- affect the mind or ways that I could do it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. But when you were at the police academy, one of the things that you learned about was various investigative techniques when you were talking to witnesses; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was taught various investigative techniques, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Everybody is.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I mean, that is standard practice whether you're in Chicago, San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York. It doesn't make any difference.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There are a series of guidelines that exist for that stuff all over the United States.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Some of it promulgated by something that's called -- I think it's the Department of Justice?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's some of the information that you study when you're at the police academy?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The DOJ [realtime transcript read in error "OJ"] procedures as they're called?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also, I think, you studied various particular issues that exist with such things as gangs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's DOJ procedures, not OJ. All right. You also dealt with such things as gangs; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you started off in your career as a police officer, you were involved with Chicago housing authority; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Chicago housing authority deals with projects?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those are closed communities?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those are communities that have folks who are pretty suspicious in it; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't generalise and say that all the folks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not all the folks, but --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But there is criminal element just like this is in the rest of the society.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the gang issue, the people who are either part of gangs or who are suspected of being a part of crimes, they're a pretty tight community, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gangs overall are a pretty community, whether it could be in the west side of Chicago or in public housing, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were in public housing -- that's what I'm dealing with for the moment.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because you were dealing with gangs; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were specifically dealing with the culture of gangs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you learned both on the street as well as when you were at the police academy, a series of investigative techniques in terms of dealing with gangs.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what I'm talking about is, more specifically, you learned how to deal with closed communities; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, in the gangs that you dealt with back in Chicago, one of the things, there was an attribute of those gangs -- some of those folks had monikers, nicknames; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the gangs in the housing projects, most of the people you're dealing with, they weren't white now, were they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on public housing, which one I was working. For example, on the south side, Lathorp did have whites in it. But overall, the higher percentage were African Americans.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one of the issues that was of a constant source of concern to you in dealing with your investigation back then, before you got over the strange and curious land of the former Yugoslavia, a place that you never knew about, was issues concerning identification; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you had to be pretty careful about the identification procedures that you dealt with when you were out on the street. True?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As well as the identification procedures that you dealt with when you were trying to identify suspects, witnesses, or anybody else; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You learned at the police academy a procedure for doing that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were learning that procedure, you were aware, as were police officers all across the United States, of the number of convictions that were obtained through wrong eyewitness identification. Weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was a pretty big issue when you were in the police academy, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, there were a series of cases you probably even discussed one of them in your academy, a case Neil versus Biggers?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I vaguely remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And one of the things you learned about was how important it was to have a fair, neutral identification process.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's no doubt about that, is there?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You went through the series of components about what would be fair, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were told by your training officers years ago what a standard -- we're talking about a standard not even of excellence but what a standard of minimum guarantees were, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those guarantees are the guarantees that you just discussed with Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, among other things --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters request the speakers not to overlap with each other, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was also the way of conducting an investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was also the way of conducting --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Conducting an investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm sure one of the things you were taught in Chicago, the same way you are taught it all over the United States, is that you were taught the importance of memorialising each and every important and critical detail involved in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you were probably given something in terms of sheets that you could use and they were called maybe same as in Chicago other places as in the United States, they're called chronos?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Stands for chronological; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you're supposed to do when you're using a chrono, is it not, is you're supposed to write down the date and the time that you have contact with regard to the particular investigation you're involved in; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you're supposed to put in that particular piece of information on that chrono, all of the important stuff that is -- that occurs; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: People you meet?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Things that they say?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How they've said it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What other leads you get?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what your impressions are?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That doesn't deviate from one place to another, does it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: These are some of the things that you were armed with when you went to Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is not something that was new to you, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. In terms of dealing with your investigative techniques, it was important, when you were back in the police academy, not when you got on the street, but when you were back in the police academy, it was important that all details were memorialised, including, for example, when you received negative information. Do you follow me?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you received information that, for example, an individual wasn't involved, that was something you're supposed to write down.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you received information that an individual wasn't identified, that was something you were supposed to memorialise; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, when you're dealing with it from the standpoint of photo line-ups or photo spreads, as I think we call them; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sure you appreciate that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When you're dealing with photo spreads, whenever an individual looks at a photo spread, whether or not there is a positive identification, a negative identification, or no identification, what you're supposed to do is you're supposed to have them sign it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Date it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Get the time that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you have in the entirety of the package, the information that you're going to give to the Prosecutor, all of the things that occurred.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So there's a full and complete dossier.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Although we wouldn't call it a dossier, would we?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We would use another word. That was something you knew before you went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now you said yesterday that when you showed somebody a photo spread, that was I guess in Kosovo and they didn't identify anybody, you did nothing. That's what you said yesterday; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe I also stated that I would document it in my notes, saying that suspect -- or witness was not able to identify any suspect in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there are several instances of that in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But you didn't do what we just talked about a second ago, did you? You didn't have them sign that document, did you, that photo spread. You didn't have them do that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had them sign it only when they identified someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did inventory the photo line-up that I had used. That would be attached to the statement, although I did not have him sign it if he didn't recognise anyone, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why not? If that was something you learned back in the police academy, if that was something you were doing in the United States, if that was something that you knew was -- and remember, we're not talking about the standard of excellence now, we're talking about minimal procedures, and now you're over in this other place where you're dealing with war crimes, why wouldn't you do that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I first got to CCIU there was different procedures in tact at the time on how we were going to do the photo spreads, as you call it. There was -- at that time they wanted us, the International Prosecutor under the case -- because they kept telling us we're dealing with Yugoslavian law, okay? And the procedures that they only wanted -- like was to circle the number, sign it and put it in; if he didn't identify anyone, just have the attachment with the case report and put in your notes or in the statement that, you know, witness was not able to identify a suspect. See, with each Prosecutor we were dealing or each case or each commander that would come in, there was always maybe a different set of rules. And that was happening and the reason for that was because you had, you know, 50 different police forces coming from all over the world working together under Yugoslavian law, and that's what we were told, at the time you're working under Yugoslavian law.
