utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself to be a pretty good cop, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I try to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You pride yourself in your work; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I try to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you learned a standard of behaviour as you talked about a second ago working on the streets in Chicago dealing with closed communities, so you had some expertise with regard to being involved in difficult situations, and are you telling us that what you did you didn't follow what you considered, yourself, to be minimal standards, because it was too confusing because there were police officers from all over the world?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I'm saying. I'm saying there was different guidelines at that time concerning the photo spreads at CCIU. At that time, they required us to just take those pictures, circle them, and which -- that's what I did. That's what I followed, you know, per my training officer at that time --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the RUC, Robin Hodgkins.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And tell us specifically if you can what was the protocol that Robin Hodgkins from the RUC gave you with regard to the use of photo spreads.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time we were told to bring in the witness, into a room. Have the photo spread already placed on the table, do not say anything. Ask him to look through all of the pictures, take his time. And at that time go ahead and circle the number and sign it, if he identified anyone. If he didn't identify anyone, take the photo line-up that you showed and place it in a -- along with the statement and make some comments on your sup report saying that he did not identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, during your investigation, did you show any photo spreads of Mr. Bala?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I'm a bit confused here. Maybe you can help me out. Being a police officer, I assume that one of the things that you do is you're pretty careful about what you sign your name to; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, that's something you know is really important?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because as a matter of fact, the information that you give to prosecuting authorities is something they're going to rely on; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you're real careful before you commit to anything?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that's something you've been doing for years?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is not something which is new to you, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Strange?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's not something which was different, for example, in Kosovo than it was when you were in Chicago, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And incidentally when you trained -- you said to us that you trained police officers; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And do you train police officers in the use of identification techniques?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What do you train them in?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Street survival, firearms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, the work that you're doing right now which -- you're a bodyguard?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, yes, you're a bodyguard. You're guarding people; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I mean close, far away, you're a bodyguard? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when you were involved -- when you were involved in -- in the interviews with folks in the ICTY, some of whom who were your buddies, and you were going over your statement --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know any of the ICTY investigators from -- that have ever interviewed them. I have never had a relationship with them. We were never in CCIU together with the ones that there were on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have contact with them?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You had some contact with them, right. I mean for example, Ole. You know Ole; right? Ole Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I met Ole here in, at The Hague. I remember I had seen him once -- I'm pretty good with faces bad with names, but I never had any personal contact with him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Written contact with him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with Ole, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when you were working up your statement and you came to this point about who you had showed suspect sheets to, the information that you just spoke about with Mr. Mansfield?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You said, and now I'm not going to deal with Mr. Limaj and I'm not going to deal with Mr. Musliu. I'm only dealing with Mr. Bala, okay?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You said: "I cannot recall how many witnesses that I personally showed the suspect sheets to, but I do recall showing" -- I will use the same name, witness A, "we also talked about another witness."

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "And we also talked about Zeledin" [phoen]; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Photos of Haradin Bala?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was a mistake I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, before we get to whether it was a mistake you made or not. It wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you then said, this is paragraph 97 --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely. If you've got it there, yes. It's your witness statement. Have you got the witness statement there? Your witness statement. I believe it is in your binder. 2003. Paragraph 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can we go into private session just for one moment so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On 97 you say: "I recall that witness A identified Bala."

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the reason that you made these mistakes was because you didn't have documents with you. You didn't have stuff to review.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as a police officer with some experience, as a police officer who knows the importance of a statement, could you explain why you didn't require a full review of the case that you'd been involved in, before you made as bold a statement - because this is a pretty bold statement here - not only do you have these witnesses being shown photo spreads that you never showed them, but you have a witness identifying my client which never happened.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as a police officer or one who exercises great care in terms of putting an investigation together, how could you let that occur?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was relying on my memory, unfortunately, and it didn't serve me right that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we're to rely on your memory with regards to the other matters that you've told us about here today to the extent that you haven't got them documented, we're supposed to rely on your memory?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which particular ones are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to get involved in the conversation you just had with Mr. Mansfield. But there were a number of occasions when we have to rely on your memory again, don't we?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, do you remember when you were putting -- and I understand you did not put the photo spreads together yourself personally. But do you remember whether or not, during the period of time that you were doing the placement of the photographs, whether or not -- because you mentioned that you would use more than one form for a photo spread?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not you put the individual who you believed to be the suspect in any particular position consistently, for example, positions 2 and 4?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would switch them around, but I can't recall exactly which one I had them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But you keep them in two positions? Or would you go to any position at all on the photo spread?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had switched I believe two, three, different positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. But you kept them in that regard consistently?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And did you have -- did you have a chart that you used so that you said that you were going to use a photo spread, for example, A, of suspect A, with this witness. And photo spread B, of suspect A, with the second witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have some kind of chart for that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So there was a way of making a determination in case the paper clip slipped off?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Or in case the stapler came loose?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So there was some way of making a determination what went with what?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I waited to see whether you were going to rush straight into something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, no. I was actually thinking about rushing into something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's break for half an hour. So we will resume on the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. With your permission, I am going to try to finish my examination by 1.15. In the event that I cannot, I am going to ask that my examination be truncated and Mr. Topolski can proceed because he cannot be here on Monday, if I have Court's permission to do that. I will try to get it done in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just move along quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I shall. I shall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated that you were involved when you were in Kosovo in actually investigating war crimes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you whether or not you were involved -- you personally were involved in investigation of war crimes concerning massacres in Fushe Kosova?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fushe Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Obri, Cikatov or Poklec?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you involved in the investigation of war crimes concerning massacres that occurred in Likoshan, Qirez, and Prekaz?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last one was?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Prekaz.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All of those are war crimes that involved Serbians.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you ever involved in any war crimes involving the investigating Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to the question about the placement of photographs in the photo spread.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I want to use the photo spread of Fatmir Limaj, if I might. And I have received permission to do so. And I would like you to go back to tab 2, if you could.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in this particular photo line-up he is in position number 1; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The other position that you had Mr. Limaj in was in position number 6; correct.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from positions number 1 and 6, you had him in no other positions, did you? You placed him in no other positions in your photo spreads, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I have -- oh, we're doing very well. I want to go back just for a moment with regard to the issue of photo spreads, eyewitness identification, information that you learned, okay.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I think we've established already that during the time that you were in the police academy the whole issue of witness identification was a pretty pressing issue throughout the United States because there were a fair number of wrongful convictions during that time that occurred as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Did you, in your classes, come across any of the studies that were done by a professor named Elizabeth Loftus?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The name doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you come across any of the studies that were done by a gentleman whose name is Gary Wells?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During your tenure with the police department, up until the present -- I assume you have some contact with the guys back in Chicago who are police. Do you still talk to them and see what's going on?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Keep up on current events?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the recommendations that were made in 2002 with regard to photo identifications?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the studies that have been done that included work by Mr. Wells specifically with regard to the state of Illinois because of some of the concerns that existed in terms of wrongful convictions as a result of faulty identifications?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not something you guys talked about, in terms of the stuff that was going on as you're administering justice or attempting to?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We weren't talking about photo spreads or the different -- I mean, I had gone back to Chicago. We were visiting. Actually, we were talking about which pub we were going to frequent to have a beer together. But the conversation of photo spreads or these authors never came up in conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the United States, were you aware of a project called the Innocence Project which dealt specifically with the issue of wrongful convictions of individuals in the United States, a lot of who have been convicted and were sentenced to death as a result of improper photo identifications?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that several people had been sentenced to death because of improper photo identification, but I'm not familiar with the cases, or -- you know, of course I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when you were doing work in the gang task force, and you said that you were involved even in homicide investigations; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I would receive a name from the detective division, or if it had just happened and I would then begin to try and locate the suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were involved in homicide investigations, especially when you were dealing with issues concerning gangs, those kind of cases had the potential of being cases in which individuals could be charged with a crime that could have as a consequence the death penalty, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in those situations, were you involved in any cases in which the issues concerning eyewitness identification and the frailties that exist with regard to them came up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the homicide investigations I wasn't involved in any photo line-ups. I had handled armed robberies, burglaries or lesser crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told us, I think yesterday, that when you were doing work with the gang task force, you even did work with murders or homicides; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I assisted -- I assisted the detective division.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So when you said even homicides, were you kind of inflating what you were doing there? You really weren't doing much homicide work?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's not fair. The answer is clear. He talked about he didn't use photo line-ups in homicides. I think that is clear from his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a police officer, somebody who is involved in -- in trying to, I would hope, you know, cut everybody a square deal, the issues that I've just been discussing with you, these are important things, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to fairly producing a photo spread for somebody to look at, did you ever discuss the following: Eyewitnesses should be told explicitly that the suspected perpetrator might not be in the line-up or photo spread and therefore they should not feel that they must make an identification? Was that ever anything you discussed?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss, when you were in the police academy when you were learning how to do this stuff, the following idea, the following notion: Eyewitnesses should be told they should not assume the person administering the line-up or photo spread knows which person is the suspect?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the police academy, yes, but it was -- I was following a different set of procedures when I was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. So what happened when you were in Kosovo which was an idea, a principle of fairness, that existed, that you'd been taught as a young officer, was not required in Kosovo and therefore you didn't do it. Right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not true. For example --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Answer that question. Answer that question. That wasn't required; right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The principle of fairness was required in all of my cases and so --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The principle that I'm just referring to right here, this one.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And because it wasn't required, you didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think I made the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am very impressed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I make it clear that I do not propose to ask this witness any questions at all and can we just go into private session for the purposes of the name, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, my name is Topolski --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I am neither from Chicago nor California. Mr. Powles and I represent Isak Musliu. Regarding the approach to the photo line-up aspect OF the investigation is the sole topic I want to deal with in the time that is left this afternoon, and I hope to finish in that time. I suggest to you that your approach to this entire investigation was a biased one. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You agree? That you were biased?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. No, No. I was impartial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Impartial. So when a witness speaks to you and you say to us this morning, as you did, it was obvious to me he was telling the truth, that is not an indicator of bias and we shouldn't so interpret it. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I had observed the contradictions and had asked for reasonable questions from him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: We'll come back to that. I suggest that your part in the entire process of the preparation and showing of photo line-ups was deeply flawed. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering the conditions that I was working with, I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I suggest that as far as you personally are concerned, you are someone who is prepared to sign inaccurate statements which purport to be true, to the best of your knowledge and recollection. That is something you have done, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not prepared to do it. I made a mistake and I did it, but it is not something that I purposely set out to do and say, I'm going to sign false statements against one; no, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You have done it more than once, haven't you, in relation to more than one subject. As Mr. Mansfield has been dealing with this morning.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was two instances in my statement made to the ICTY where I had made the mistake, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You do realise, don't you, with particular regard to the case against Isak Musliu, how important identification is?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you accept as a proposition that identification procedures during the course of your investigation into this case were - and I quote - "not always followed in the correct way"? Do you accept that as a proposition or not?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure I used, according to the ones that you stated, or the procedures I used at the time they were in effect at CCIU? I don't understand the question. If the procedures that you're stating, yes, they were incorrect. At the time that I'm following the procedures at CCIU, they were correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: This quotation - and I will come to its source later - can only be referring to activity on the ground in Kosovo at a time when you were present, and the quotation only relating to that can only mean what it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. says, that the person saying this was of the view that your procedures you and your colleagues were adopting were not always followed in the correct way. Do you accept that or do you reject that as a proposition?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to reject that because if the procedures that you're saying are the ones that we were using at CCIU at the time, you know, one minute we had a -- we were told we were under Yugoslavian law and the case would be presented to an investigating judge under Yugoslavian law. The best example I can give this is, when the witness took us to the crime scene, and we saw protruding bones coming out we had to have an investigating judge there to sign the proper paperwork in order to begin even to secure the crime scene. We could not even secure the crime scene because under Yugoslavian law that was left up to the investigating judge. So, there were certain procedures that we were following that where from the Brits, maybe there was some procedures being followed by Yugoslavian law. So there was some confusion on that part, yes, I will admit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You were there from 2001 through to 2002; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At CCIU I was. I was in Kosovo from 2000 though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Where were the cases that were the product of all of these investigations being tried?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there any other cases with which you were involved in investigating tried here, in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was the first one I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: This was the first one.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: When you got there and took up your investigation into the case of Limaj an others, did you understand - I won't use the word appreciate - did you understand that it was this Tribunal who was going to be trying any case that emanated from your investigation?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not know if it was going to come to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You did not know that alleged war crimes against Fatmir Limaj and others were going to come to this Tribunal. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a chance that ICTY might pick it up, but that was not at all a guarantee. We first had approach and begin the investigation under Yugoslavian law. That's how it was explained to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: As far as practice and procedure is concerned, you referred a little earlier on today to there being different guidelines. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I want to know this, if you can help, please, Mr. Kereakes: Were these guidelines in written form?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Were they, therefore, as a result of formal briefings or informal conversations between colleagues?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Both. At formal briefings that you participated in regarding "different guidelines," who would conduct that briefing?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our commander or possibly even the International Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you be good enough to identify the names of anyone you can remember conducting such a briefing, please.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dennis Sherman, and also Brian Cox, CCIU commanders. Also International Prosecutors, Michael Hartman, and a couple of the other names escape me for now, but they could be found in a -- my supplemental report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would there be any written hand-outs given by the briefers to the briefees at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you make notes about what --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I believe in a couple of instances there could have been a hand-out given. From now on we will, in order to exhume mass grave you must have an investigating judge --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, sorry to interrupt you. As I said at the beginning I'm focussing, please, on photo line-ups, practice and procedure.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: All I'm going to be talking about for the next 20 minutes or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: So in that regard only if you wouldn't mind focussing. Do you recollect any written hand-outs by way of a guideline regarding practice and procedure on photo line-ups or spreadsheets?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: No. Did you make any notes yourself of these briefings that you attended on this subject?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Why did you volunteer for this work in Kosovo? Why?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why did I go to Kosovo to work?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to try something different. I had been in Chicago for the last ten years, and I thought that it would be kind of a challenging to go to a different country and attempt a different type of line of police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You didn't know where Yugoslavia was? On the map. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your name is Greek.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You have family in Greece?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You're aware of the ancient and historical association between Greeks and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Just general sympathy is concerned, Mr. Kereakes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware that -- of any sympathies of Greeks and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And you certainly didn't have any particular sympathies yourself for either side in the conflict when you went there. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Utterly objective and open-minded?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: When dealing with surviving crime victims as a serving police officer in the United States, would you call them witnesses or victims? When you dealt with them?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Victims. What about witnesses to crimes, who may not have themselves been victims? What do they get called in your vocabulary when you're dealing with them?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: There is a certain difference between someone who is a witness and someone who is a victim?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: As far as familiarity with the events that you were dealing with and the investigation that you were in due course to become a member of a team with, regarding that aspect of the matter, February 2001 you joined the team investigating this case. Yes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you take steps to familiarise yourself with the case thus far?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you take steps to familiarise yourself with the identities of the known suspects at that point, February 2001?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Was Isak Musliu a suspect in February 2001?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took the case over and I read the initial statement, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Was Fatmir Limaj by name a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if the other witnesses who had already been recorded if their name had ever been mention; no, I can't remember that. But I know from witness A's statement that name had not been mentioned, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: His was not the only witness, was he? Even in February 2001. Mr. A.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the only name that you became aware of in those early days of reading the papers, looking at reports, familiarising yourself with the file, the only named suspect you can recollect was Isak Musliu? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't recall if the other suspect's name, or at least one of the other suspect's name -- no, there was actually another suspect's name in that case. I don't know if I can say it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, not in open session you can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I just try to clarify. I think there might be a mistake. There's been talk of the witness taking over this investigation in February 2001. I believe his testimony was July 2001, when he began working on the case we're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, of course, Mr. Nicholls can give the evidence if he want, but this witness has just accepted it was February 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: So which is it, Mr. Kereakes, February or July?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm confused if you're talking about a particular statement or a particular time that I had been working on the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry if my English isn't plain enough for you. I asked you when you started to take up work in the investigation of this case, and I suggested February 2001 and you agreed with me. Would you like to change that now?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I was assigned at CCIU -- or July -- or February of 2001, but that doesn't mean that I took over the case in February of 2001. I would have to look at my notes, and I could tell you the exact time I began reading this case file, but I believe that when you mentioned that date, you were referring to the different cases when I first began February of 2001 in CCIU.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Let's move on. When looking at the question of the compilation of photo line-ups and the like, did you investigate whether there were any contemporary video footages available of any of the people you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not find any video footage of the people I was investigating.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did anyone look for it, that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did anyone do a search of newspaper archives like, for example, Koha Ditore, looking for photographs of people who were known or suspected of being involved in these war crimes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm not going to take you through the evidence you've given already and the answers you've already given to Mr. Mansfield on a variety of topics concerning practice and procedure. I want to move on to deal with the specific sheet behind our tab 1, if you would be good enough, please, Mr. Kereakes. This is Isak Musliu?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you first appreciate that Isak Musliu, throughout the entirety of the war, was bearded?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a couple of the statements it was mentioned that he was bearded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you aware of those statements before you showed witnesses photo line-ups of him?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me it would be an utterly valueless exercise in showing a witness a line-up of an utterly clean-shaven Isak Musliu if you knew he would be bearded at the time we are dealing with? Worthless, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I wouldn't say it was worthless.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: What would you say about it then?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If no pictures were available of the suspect wearing a beard in our database or at other times, I think it is very valuable to show a picture of the -- in a photo line-up of him clean shaven if that's the only one available. We didn't have, you know, access to him with a picture with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit's number 81. Could we put it on the ELMO, please. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: There's an arrow pointing to a gentleman there; I'm not interested in him. The man behind him, over his right shoulder, that's Isak Musliu. Have you ever seen this photograph before?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree he has a beard and a rather significant one in that photograph, if that be him? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you saying the subject to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: The left of the photograph as you look at it. Over Fatmir Limaj's right shoulder; your left as you look at it.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: The little chap. With the gun across his chest. That's Isak Musliu. Do you see he has a beard?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Never seen this photograph before?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You were asked a number of questions about your dealings with the witness A, and I too ask you, please, Mr. Kereakes, and I know it is difficult, be careful about no name.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you take it from me that the date you showed this particular witness the photo line-up of Isak Musliu was the 17th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did anyone, throughout any of your time at the CCIU in Kosovo investigating these matters, with regard to identification procedures, ever talk about the possibility of identification parades as opposed to line-ups of photographs? Anyone talk about that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said identification parades?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know what they are?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: In American, they're called line-ups.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. You've seen the movie The Usual Suspects?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Line-ups. Anyone talk about line-ups as a possibility of a method of identification?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there any?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason for that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Namely?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I at the time did not want to bring in the suspects. I didn't have the facility to secure the safety of my witnesses nor did I have a room where I could secure the witness on one side without exposing him to language assistance, security guards, so that way they will be able to tell that here you are bringing in this suspect and the witness together, so I felt that would jeopardise, because the biggest common denominator we had was the fear that the witnesses felt of the suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kereakes, of course not. You're not going to put Mr. A, right in front of -- physically in front of in touching distance --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I didn't have a room for that at CCI --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you telling this Court that nowhere in the former state of Yugoslavia was an identification suite where a witness could be brought behind a frosted glass to look through to see a suspect in a line-up? Is that the -- is that the case?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that there was no place at CCIU or even a special operations compound that we were provided that I could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Because you see, at the time you showed Mr. A the photo line-up of Isak Musliu, 17th of August, 2001, he was a serious suspect, Musliu, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time is when the witness A gave me the information, but I had already read previous statements on him. So that's when I had identified him. As far as him being a serious suspect he was a suspect in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: No. I used the word serious advisedly, Mr. Kereakes. He had been interviewed three months before that in May. He had been arrested and interviewed by UNMIK. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't find that out till later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you seriously telling us that you're conducting these procedures with witnesses like A, and you're not even aware as an investigator on the team that Musliu had been arrested and interviewed?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If their particular arrest report had been in my -- a file at that time. I don't remember that being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, here is the witness statement. I hold it in my hand of the interview on the 24th of May of 2001. Where, other than in the files you were dealing with, would this document be?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Of course you can. 03231634, I think. My client's interview with UNMIK, May. Three months before you are with Mr. A, showing him photos. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Right. So he was a serious suspect, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I have that back? Two more matters. Were you involved in the investigation of the case that brought a man called Agim Murtezi to this Court?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His name had been mentioned in several witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me his case represents one of the greatest possible failures of identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have anything to do with those.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in that arrest or actually --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Because of course they brought the wrong man here, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I said I would come back to the question of the reference you make regarding a particular person who was obviously to you lying. Remember I said I would come back to it and I do, Mr. Kereakes. You spoke in evidence when Mr. Nicholls was asking you questions this morning of the purpose, as you saw it, in confronting one witness with another.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Physically bringing them into a room together to, as it were, thrash it out between them?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would never have used the word "thrashed."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, I don't mean it to have physical connotations, Mr. Kereakes. I don't -- this is not a arm wrestling contest. To bring them face to face, to quote you, so the truth would somehow come out.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Isn't that what a court is for?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you think it is an appropriate thing for a police officer to be doing with witnesses?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I felt it was something that should be done considering the fact that he knew -- the witness A knew this particular witness that was not being truthful or had many contradictions. So, yes, at that time I felt there was -- I thought maybe the scene of the -- of witness A, and maybe recalling some of it could actually have the truth come out. Can I turn on my video monitor in case I'm talking too fast, my monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. I find myself in a bit of an awkward position. But I'm going to have to object to the last answer because, once again, there is no basis for his conclusion the witness was not being truthful, which was the same thing I objected to before when Mr. Nicholls raised the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think it is the fault of the question. It's the direction the answer took but...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have serious personal problems with CCIU commander Dennis Sherman?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At one point I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Were those problems so severe that you became aware that he was ordering people not to talk to you? Colleagues?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this an operation involving a search of a TMK location that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was told this was national security, so I don't know if I'm allowed to speak about this, so... I don't know if at that time it involved certain intelligence agencies, and I don't know if I'm allowed to speak about it at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I won't pursue it. I just wanted to establish the basis of the suggestions I was making regarding Mr. Sherman. Just finally this: Do you agree that all of the witnesses that you were dealing with in these photo line-up exercises, as well as the suspects themselves, all came from the same geographical area south-west of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree that some of the witnesses with whom you were dealing knew the suspects from before the war?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that the five photographs of the gentleman I have shown you on -- behind tab number 1, the Musliu tab, were all serving police officers in Ferizaj, as was Mr. Musliu? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That all of them were police officers in Ferizaj. This I did not know. I knew they were all KPS officers. But that they were serving in Ferizaj, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Would that have concerned you to put six five men, plus Musliu all from the same area, all in the same job, all on the same line-up sheet? Would you have done that if you had known what I just suggested to you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have tried to get KPS officers probably from all different parts of Kosovo, but I didn't think of it as -- I didn't know at that time when we pulled these pictures they were all from Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I suggested at the outset of my cross-examination that you were careless in the proper meaning of that word throughout this entire investigation and your part in it. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering the conditions I had, I would have to disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll be very quick, Witness, we only have a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You've been asked repeatedly on cross-examination whether you ever instructed witnesses when you were showing them a photo line-up, U-1 or U-2, whether you told them that the suspect might not be in the photo line-up. Now the flip side: Did you ever tell any witness that a suspect was included in the photo line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just never instructed them on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Forgive me, Witness. I realise we are pressed for time, or you are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I asked you if you remember a question indicating that when the matter was investigated, after you had left the investigation, no officer could find any line-up relating to Fatmir Limaj, the U-2 line-up, in which he was placed at number 3. All right?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In other words, where witnesses claimed to have picked him out of position 3 - there are two, I'm not mentioning their names - there are at least two, no copy of that photo line-up has ever been found, and no other line-up done in preparation for these processes has ever been found. Do you follow? That's the position.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Now, on the back of that, you were asked by Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith, who sits to my right here, a fellow American, he asked you what the positions were in very clear terms, in which Fatmir Limaj was placed. And the answer you gave then was that apart from positions 1 and 6, that you did not have Fatmir Limaj in any other position. You gave a very clear answer to that. Now, are you wanting to change that?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I would like to change is, if that's what I said, is that it's possible he was 1 or 3, or maybe even another position, because at the time when we had these created I had told -- I had instructed the photo guy to try to put him in different positions. And those were placed in a sheet under U-2 or U-1. So it is possible that he was in a different position and not just 1 and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, of course, anything is possible, but when you were asked the question, it's very clear - we have it on screen at the moment - the question was: Apart from positions 1 and 6, you had him in no other position, did you? You placed him in no other position in your photo spreads, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, could I have a line reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Line 15 on 104. 104, line 15 is the question through to 17 and the answer is 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In other words, you made no qualification that, oh, well, maybe you had to put him in another position just in case witnesses passed in the corridor or anything like that. In other words, would it be fair to say you have no recollection, at all, of putting Fatmir Limaj in position 3, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not true. I didn't tell you about passing the people in the corridor and the reason for that, I wasn't asked. But, is it possible that he was placed in a different position? Now that I think about -- yes, it is possible, because the photo line-ups that were developed by someone else, I had specifically asked them to, you know, take -- take the position of the suspect move them around so that way there is no way that one witness is telling the other witness, Hey, pick number 4, or pick number 2. Is it possible that another witness -- I mean, is it possible that another line-up was underneath? Yes, it is. It is very possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, anything is possible. But do you understand that the matter has been thoroughly investigated and there is no example of any sheet compiled by anyone in relation to Fatmir Limaj in which he's at position 3.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm missing my photo line-ups also. They're not here. They're also not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the ones attached to the statements?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Two of them. In fact, there are no none attached to statements that have survived. You can't explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think we're getting passed the re-cross that was opened up by His Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hadn't discerned that yet, Mr. Nicholls. But the time will bring it to an end shortly, if nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. See the point I'm reaching is: Never mind the ones that have all gone missing that were supposed to be attached to statements, you can't help us about that.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I'm now dealing with is your suggestion that the possible way in which Fatmir Limaj may have reached position 3 is that you would have prepared examples of that ready for a witness if you needed to use it. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. No examples of prepared line-ups, unattached to statements, have survived. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I'm going to suggest to you, therefore, there were no line-ups prepared by you in which he was other than in position 1 and 6. And that is what you told Mr. Gregor Smith.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But thinking about it, it is very possible that line-ups were created with a different number, just like I can't remember every number that Isak Musliu was also too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there anything you would want to take it further with?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kereakes, that concludes the questions to be asked of you. We've run over time. So I can't delay now, but thank you for your attendance and you're now free to return to your other activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume on Monday at 2.15.
